title: Safety and efficacy of rapamycin on healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL Trial Results | medRxiv
abstract: # Safety and efficacy of rapamycin on healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL Trial Results. We performed a 48-week double-blinded, randomized, and placebo-controlled decentralized study (Participatory Evaluation of Aging with Rapamycin for Longevity [PEARL]; NCT04488601; registration date 2020-07-28) to evaluate the safety and efficacy of rapamycin in mitigating clinical signs of aging in a normative aging cohort. We did not detect significant differences in safety blood biomarkers, or moderate to severe AEs between the rapamycin treatment groups and placebo after 48 weeks. Additionally, some individuals receiving rapamycin experienced significant improvements in body composition metrics that were associated with beneficial changes in gut health and lipid metabolism. I understand that all clinical trials and any other prospective interventional studies must be registered with an ICMJE-approved registry, such as ClinicalTrials.gov. All data produced in the present study are available upon reasonable request to the authors. Safety and efficacy of rapamycin on healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL Trial Results.
